title: Nasal [ɑ̃] — an, am, en, em (set 3)
focus: These spellings all make the nasal vowel [ɑ̃], as in « enfant ». In Québec it is usually pronounced further forward in the mouth than in Paris, so it can sound close to a Parisian « in » — listen for that. Careful: the verb ending -ent (« ils chantent ») is silent, never nasal, and a following vowel or doubled n/m cancels the nasal (« banane », « Jeanne »).

sentences.fr: Au print[em]ps, il fait doux et il pleut souv[en]t.
sentences.en: In spring, it's mild and it often rains.

sentences.fr: [En] été, les [en]f[an]ts jouent à la plage.
sentences.en: In summer, the children play at the beach.

sentences.fr: L'automne est très beau d[an]s les Laur[en]tides.
sentences.en: Autumn is very beautiful in the Laurentians.

sentences.fr: [En] hiver, il fait froid et il y a du v[en]t.
sentences.en: In winter, it's cold and windy.

sentences.fr: Mam[an] dit : « Mets ta tuque et tes g[an]ts ! »
sentences.en: Mom says: "Put on your toque and your gloves!"
